Marinated Olives for Saturnalia

Served at: Saturnalia

Serves 6-8 as an appetizerPrep 15 min

Olives were a staple in ancient Roman diets, enjoyed by all social classes. During Saturnalia, the festive winter solstice celebration, tables would have been laden with simple yet delicious fare, and marinated olives would have been a welcome savory bite, perfect for sharing among friends and family as they feasted and exchanged gifts.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (300g) mixed olives (e.g., Kalamata, Castelvetrano, or a mix of black and green)
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) extra virgin olive oil
  • 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced or minced
  • 1 sprig fresh rosemary, leaves stripped and roughly chopped
  • 1 sprig fresh thyme, leaves stripped
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • Zest of 1/2 lemon
  • Pinch of red pepper flakes (optional)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Method

  1. Drain the olives from their brine and rinse them gently under cold water. Pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel.
  2. In a medium bowl, combine the drained olives with the extra virgin olive oil, sliced or minced garlic, chopped fresh rosemary, fresh thyme leaves, dried oregano, lemon zest, and red pepper flakes (if using).
  3. Toss everything together thoroughly to ensure the olives are well coated with the oil and seasonings.
  4. Season with a pinch of salt and freshly ground black pepper, adjusting to your taste. Remember that olives are already salty.
  5. Cover the bowl and let the olives marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld.
  6. Before serving, bring the olives to room temperature for about 30 minutes to enhance their flavor. Serve them in a small bowl with toothpicks or alongside other appetizers.

Tips

  • For an extra layer of flavor, gently warm the olive oil with the garlic and herbs for a few minutes before adding to the olives, then let it cool before combining.
  • Experiment with different varieties of olives; a mix of briny, buttery, and firm olives adds textural and flavor complexity.
  • These marinated olives can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week.
